AfriScan · Malawi · Wayleaves, reserves and project land

Know what has been built inside your wayleaves and reserves in Malawi

We map structures, excavations, cleared ground and new tracks along power lines, roads and railways, and across project areas in Malawi. Each structure gets coordinates and its distance to your line or boundary, each 500 m of route gets a rating, and dated surveys show what is new since your cut-off date. Satellite first, and a person reviews every result before you receive the PDF report and GIS files.

Our published sample is from Mozambique: the route of a high-pressure gas pipeline, with its 100 m band, on a Copernicus Sentinel-2 scene of 2 August 2026. Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2026.

The rules behind the work Electricity Act ss.39 and 41 · Public Roads Act s.10 · Land Survey Act s.42 · Civil Aviation Act 2017 · Data Protection Act 2024 · Environment Management Act 2016 · IFC Performance Standard 5

The widths are in the law

Lines, roads and the date that counts

The Electricity Act and the Public Roads Act say what may stand beside a line or a road, and resettlement plans fix the date after which new occupation is not compensated. Each needs a record of what is on the ground.

Electricity Act, s.41

Power-line wayleaves

“Except with the permission of the licensee, no person shall erect any building or structure in the wayleave.” For one put up after the line, the licensee may ask for it to be removed or adjusted, and then apply to the energy regulator, MERA, for an order. A recent 400 kV line from Mozambique was planned with a 55 m wayleave.

Read

Public Roads Act, s.10

Road reserves

Road reserves are 60 m for main roads, 36 m for secondary, tertiary and district roads and 18 m for branch and estate roads. Putting up or altering a structure, planting a tree or bush, or preparing new land for cultivation in a reserve needs the highway authority’s written consent.

Read

Resettlement plans

Cut-off dates

Malawian resettlement plans tie the cut-off date to the census and asset inventory. People who occupy the project area after it are not eligible for compensation or resettlement assistance, so the date needs a record of what stood there.

Read

Why it matters now

New lines, busy reserves and corridors to the coast

Malawi’s power and road links to Mozambique are being built and upgraded now, and the land beside them changes between patrols.

400 kV · August 2026

Power from Mozambique

A 400 kV interconnector from Mozambique was energised in August 2026, with commercial trading waiting on tariff agreements. On its Malawian section the resettlement census, in April and May 2019, covered the project-affected people in its 55 m wayleave; the resettlement plan relocates the houses in it and allows low-lying crops, but no trees, under the line. A wayleave cleared for construction does not stay clear by itself.

Zambia · Tanzania

More interconnectors to route

Interconnectors to Zambia and to Tanzania are at feasibility stage, and grant funding to update the feasibility and ESIA studies for the 400 kV Tanzanian line was announced in July 2025. Route options compared by the structures they affect, and a dated baseline before the census, are most useful at this stage.

November 2025

Campaigns against wayleave encroachment

The national utility ran a two-month campaign in the Southern Region against vandalism and rising wayleave encroachment, working through more than 100 Traditional Authorities and over 2,000 Group Village Heads and urging people not to build or farm under power lines.

June 2026

Farming in road reserves

The Roads Authority is running nationwide sensitisation against farming in road reserves, working with district councils and traditional leaders. Meetings like these go further with a map of where the structures and cleared ground are, stretch by stretch.

What you receive

One register per route: located, measured, dated and reviewed

  • Each structure listed with an ID, its distance to the line or boundary, its band, its chainage and its coordinates in WGS84 and UTM.
  • Each 500 m of route rated high, medium or low for encroachment density, by a count rule, so your officers know which stretches to visit first. It is not a safety rating.
  • New and removed structures between dated surveys, flagged automatically and confirmed by a reviewer, with before-and-after views.
  • Cleared ground, new tracks and fresh excavations near the line, flagged for a check on the ground.
  • The imagery named, and dated where the source gives a date.
  • A PDF report with maps, the segment table and the coordinate register, with GeoPackage, GeoJSON, KMZ and Shapefile layers and an interactive map file.

Project land and resettlement

Fix the cut-off date on a dated record

Malawi has no stand-alone resettlement statute. Resettlement follows the Constitution, the Lands Acquisition and Compensation Act, the Land Act 2016, the Customary Land Act 2016 and, for roads, the Public Roads Act, with the National Land Policy 2002 and lender standards such as IFC Performance Standard 5 alongside.

The glossary of the resettlement plan for a recent 400 kV line defines the cut-off date as the date the census and asset inventory of affected people were completed; people occupying the project area after it are not eligible for compensation or resettlement assistance. A road-corridor plan disclosed in September 2026 applied a cut-off date of 30 April 2023, with its census in 2023 and valuation and verification in 2025.

That gap between the census and implementation is where a dated record helps: a baseline register on imagery captured as close to the cut-off date as the archive allows, then a comparison showing what is new since. Prescribed projects also need an approved environmental and social impact assessment before they go ahead (Environment Management Act 2016, s.31; approvals by MEPA), and a dated structure baseline feeds straight into it. Critical-minerals projects bring large land footprints in farmed areas.

For RAP, ESIA and lender teams

  • A reviewed, dated structure layer across the footprint, for the census team to start from
  • The imagery date stated; never map-service basemap tiles
  • New and removed structures since the cut-off date, during implementation
  • It supports the census and asset inventory; it does not replace them

Our standard

Land and assets, for fair and documented processes

AfriScan maps what is on the land: structures, cleared ground, excavations, tracks and vegetation change. We do not identify, count or follow people. Our registers support compensation, engagement, legal and community processes; they are not prepared for evictions, and whether a structure may stay is for you and the authorities to decide.

Checked by a person

Every automatic result is reviewed by a person before delivery. What the imagery cannot settle goes on a list for a check on the ground.

Honest about theft

Satellites cannot see theft or vandalism. We map land change so your patrols know where to look.

Dated imagery for cut-off dates

Cut-off baselines use imagery with a known capture date, from a satellite scene or a drone survey, never map-service basemap tiles.

On a schedule, not in real time

Re-surveys follow a schedule agreed with you, set by when new imagery is available and by rainy-season cloud, with a notice after each one.

Satellite first, drones under MCAA authorisation

Two ways to see the ground, and what each needs

Satellite screening. A survey starts from your route or boundary file and dated satellite imagery, open building datasets or imagery you already hold. It involves no flights over your site, and it covers a whole line or road, including stretches far from any depot.

Drone detail. Where a stretch needs more detail than satellite imagery shows, a drone survey captures it, subject to the approvals and security clearances each job requires. In Malawi that means written authorisation from the Malawi Civil Aviation Authority for the operation, 30 days’ notice of the aerial survey to the Surveyor General, a drone registered with the Surveyor General for survey and mapping work, and a deposit of the photographs and data within 30 days of completion. Every drone proposal names who will fly and the approvals its flights need, and builds those lead times into the schedule.

Drone law in Malawi

Why there are no drone regulations yet, the Civil Aviation Act authorisation, the Land Survey Act notice and deposit, protected places, data rules and a checklist for clients, as of 27 September 2026.

Corridors that start in Mozambique

One route, two countries’ rules

Malawi’s 400 kV interconnector comes in from Mozambique, and its railway links to the Nacala line, the rail route through Mozambique to the port of Nacala. For a route that crosses the border, the proposal covers both sides, with the widths that apply in each country. On the Mozambican side those are the Land Law’s partial protection zones, such as the 50 m strip beside power lines and railways, and the servitudes in Mozambican law, set out on our Mozambique pages in English and Portuguese.

The Mozambique site · Power lines in Mozambique · The 50 m partial protection zone

Where we do not send field or drone teams

  • In Mozambique: the areas where the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office advises against all or all but essential travel (advice of 20 August 2026): Cabo Delgado province, Memba and Eráti in Nampula, and Mecula and Marrupa in Niassa.
  • In Malawi: no part of the country is under an FCDO warning against travel (advice updated 3 July 2026). Drone flights still stay away from State, military and police sites, border posts and borderlands, and artisanal pits, and we do not work on the disputed Lake Malawi boundary, on contested evictions or in displacement camps.

Frequently asked questions

Which widths do you measure in Malawi?

The ones that apply to your asset. For roads we use the reserve the Public Roads Act lists for the road class: 60 m for a main road, 36 m for secondary, tertiary and district roads and 18 m for branch and estate roads, centred on the carriageway unless the Minister directs otherwise by Gazette notice (s.10(2)). Wayleave widths depend on the line: a recent 400 kV line from Mozambique was planned with a 55 m wayleave, and we quote no standard width for lower voltages, so send the width for each line or section. Up to six widths can be reported in one survey.

Does satellite screening need MCAA authorisation or the Surveyor General's notice?

Satellite screening involves no flights over your site, so no aircraft is operated in Malawi for it. The Land Survey Act requires 30 days’ notice to the Surveyor General before an aerial survey, and it defines “survey” to include aerial surveys without defining “aerial survey”. Whether that reaches the analysis of satellite imagery is a question for your counsel, and our proposals flag it. Drone stretches are planned separately, subject to the approvals and security clearances each job requires.

Can you tell us which structures are unlawful?

No. We record what stands where, and on which imagery date. Whether a structure in a wayleave had the licensee’s permission, or one in a road reserve the highway authority’s written consent, is for you and the authorities to decide. The register gives your wayleave and reserve officers a dated, located list to start from.

Can the register be used to demarcate customary land or fix a boundary?

No. Under the Land Survey Regulations 2020, customary-estate demarcation uses orthophotos, aerial and satellite images and maps approved by the Surveyor General (regs 92 and 93), and boundary work is for a land surveyor. Our registers are monitoring and planning records built from imagery, not survey plans.

Do you detect vandalism or theft on lines, cables and railways?

No. Satellites cannot see theft or vandalism. We map land change, such as new structures, tracks, cleared ground and fresh excavations near your line, cable or railway, so your patrols know where to look.

Does the Data Protection Act 2024 apply to this work?

It can. Imagery of homes, census lists and lists of project-affected persons can be personal data. Registration with the Data Protection Authority applies to anyone processing the personal data of more than 10,000 people resident in Malawi, or data of significance to the economy, society or security of Malawi (s.41). A breach must be notified to the Authority within 72 hours (s.36), and personal data may leave Malawi only where the recipient gives adequate protection or a s.39(4) condition applies, and the basis must be recorded (ss.38 to 40). Our registers describe structures and carry no names, and each proposal says who is the controller and who is the processor.

Map the wayleave or reserve before the next campaign, not after it.

Send the line, road or project boundary (KML, KMZ, GeoJSON, Shapefile, GPX or GeoPackage), the district and the widths that matter: the wayleave width for each line section, the reserve width for each road class, or your project footprint and its cut-off date. We reply by email with a scope, an imagery plan and a written proposal.
